back: The [[imp:sum of all data entries]] divided by the number of entries.
Sample mean: $ \bar{x} = \frac{\sum x}{n} $; Population mean: $ \mu = \frac{\sum x}{N} $.
Uses every value; sensitive to outliers.
The [[imp:middle value]] when data are ordered.
Odd $ n $: middle entry. Even $ n $: average of two middle entries.
Resistant to outliers; often preferred for skewed data.
cards.front: Define [[kw:median]] and how to find it.

back: The value(s) that occur [[imp:most frequently]].
Can be unimodal, bimodal, multimodal, or no mode at all.
The only measure of central tendency that works for qualitative data.
Mean: $ \approx 527.9 $.
Median: $ 427 $ (middle of ordered list).
Mode: $ 397 $ (appears twice).
cards.front: Flight prices: $388, 397, 397, 427, 432, 782, 872$. Find mean, median, mode.
What happens to the mean when an [[kw:outlier]] is present?
back: The mean is [[imp:pulled toward the outlier]].
If the outlier is very high, the mean overestimates the center.
The median stays near the bulk of the data.

cards.front: Ages of 20 students (including one 65‑year‑old). Mean = 23.8, Median = 21.5, Mode = 20. Which measure best describes the typical age?
back: [[imp:Median (21.5)]] because the outlier (65) inflates the mean.
Mode (20) also works but median better represents the center.
Mean where some values contribute more than others.
Formula: $ \bar{x} = \frac{\sum (x \cdot w)}{\sum w} $.
Example: course grades with different weights for tests, homework, etc.
Multiply each score by its weight, sum them: $ 86\cdot0.50 + 96\cdot0.15 + 82\cdot0.20 + 98\cdot0.10 + 100\cdot0.05 = 88.6 $.
Sum of weights = 1. Weighted mean = 88.6.
cards.front: Calculate the weighted mean: test (86, weight 0.50), final (82, weight 0.20), homework (100, weight 0.05), etc.
How do you approximate the mean from a [[kw:grouped frequency distribution]]?
back: Use class [[imp:midpoints]] as $ x $, frequencies as $ f $.
Formula: $ \bar{x} \approx \frac{\sum (x \cdot f)}{n} $ where $ n = \sum f $.
Only an approximation because raw data are lost.

cards.front: Internet sessions: midpoint 12.5 (f=6), 24.5 (f=10), 36.5 (f=13). Find grouped mean if total n=50 and $ \sum x f = 2089$.
back: Grouped mean = $ 2089 / 50 = 41.8 $ minutes.
Represents the approximate average time spent online.

cards.front: Describe a [[kw:symmetric distribution]] and the relationship among mean, median, mode.
back: [[imp:Mirror image]] on both sides of center.
Mean ≈ Median ≈ Mode (if unimodal).
Example: heights of adult men.
[[imp:Tail extends to the right]].
Mean > Median > Mode (usually).
Example: personal income (few very high earners).
[[imp:Tail extends to the left]].
Mean < Median < Mode (usually).
Example: age at death (most die older, few die young).
All classes have [[imp:approximately equal frequencies]].
Rectangular shape; no distinct mode.
Mean and median are near the center.

cards.front: Blueprint: How do you choose the best measure of central tendency?
back: Understand: examine shape, check for outliers.
Solve: symmetric/no outliers → mean; skewed/outliers → median; qualitative → mode.
Conclude: report measure with interpretation.
